after.label: Chapter2 prescient dependency: canonical Bregman algebra and real proximal step
after.plain: One canonical total real function Dψ(a,b)=ψ(a)-ψ(b)-Dψ(b)[a-b], using the actual Frechet derivative fderiv of ψ. The second argument is the base. At a nondifferentiable base fderiv defaults to zero; this total algebraic formula alone is not a source differentiability, positivity, metric or separation theorem. The core uses any real normed vector space; only the gradient conversion needs a complete real inner-product space. The source is finite Euclidean, ψ:X->R strictly convex/differentiable on intX; source-domain and ambient-extension locality are not silently identified. The supplied p belongs to V and actually minimizes f(z)+ηinverse Dψ(z,x) there; f is real convex on the same V, η>0, and ψ is ambient differentiable at BOTH x and p. x may be outside V. No loss derivative, ψ convexity/strictness, closedness, coercivity or existence theorem is required by this real helper. It concludes the comparison for every u in V with both negative residuals retained. Nonnegative residual values require separate convexity hypotheses; they cannot be discarded from this theorem alone. Differentiate only h(z)=ηinverse Dψ(z,x) at the selected minimum p. Its derivative is ηinverse(Dψ(p)-Dψ(x)). The accepted real nonsmooth convex-minimizer comparison gives f(p)-f(u)<=ηinverse(Dψ(p)-Dψ(x))[u-p]. Multiply by positive η and use the three-point identity with (p,x,u), obtaining Dψ(u,x)-Dψ(u,p)-Dψ(p,x). The previous-base derivative hypothesis is retained for source validity even though the fixed dual map is already linear in this proof. This is an actual-minimum comparison, not an assumed regret/stability bound or a sequence construction. Two compiled public Test families prove actual strict convexity, polynomial derivatives and minimizing conditions: ψ(z)=z^4/4+z^2/2 with nonsmooth abs loss, center1/2 and minimum0; and ψ(z)=z^2/2 on[0,1] with center-1 outsideV and boundary minimum0. The ordered nonquadratic divergences are9/64 and11/64. Each universal comparison and separately selected final numerical proof branch retains actual public proximal_one_step VALUE; final bounds -1/2<=-5/16 and -1/2<=1/2 use equality transport of that comparison. Divergence formulas also use actual public gradient conversion. Nonnegative has a full generic public VALUE witness, with no claimed concrete Test VALUE use. These are illustrative instances, not new printed results, an existence theorem or a causal algorithm.

after.proof_idea: Differentiate only h(z)=ηinverse Dψ(z,x) at the selected minimum p. Its derivative is ηinverse(Dψ(p)-Dψ(x)). The accepted real nonsmooth convex-minimizer comparison gives f(p)-f(u)<=ηinverse(Dψ(p)-Dψ(x))[u-p]. Multiply by positive η and use the three-point identity with (p,x,u), obtaining Dψ(u,x)-Dψ(u,p)-Dψ(p,x). The previous-base derivative hypothesis is retained for source validity even though the fixed dual map is already linear in this proof. This is an actual-minimum comparison, not an assumed regret/stability bound or a sequence construction.
after.lean_notes: One canonical total real function Dψ(a,b)=ψ(a)-ψ(b)-Dψ(b)[a-b], using the actual Frechet derivative fderiv of ψ. The second argument is the base. At a nondifferentiable base fderiv defaults to zero; this total algebraic formula alone is not a source differentiability, positivity, metric or separation theorem. The core uses any real normed vector space; only the gradient conversion needs a complete real inner-product space. The source is finite Euclidean, ψ:X->R strictly convex/differentiable on intX; source-domain and ambient-extension locality are not silently identified. The supplied p belongs to V and actually minimizes f(z)+ηinverse Dψ(z,x) there; f is real convex on the same V, η>0, and ψ is ambient differentiable at BOTH x and p. x may be outside V. No loss derivative, ψ convexity/strictness, closedness, coercivity or existence theorem is required by this real helper. It concludes the comparison for every u in V with both negative residuals retained. Nonnegative residual values require separate convexity hypotheses; they cannot be discarded from this theorem alone. Two compiled public Test families prove actual strict convexity, polynomial derivatives and minimizing conditions: ψ(z)=z^4/4+z^2/2 with nonsmooth abs loss, center1/2 and minimum0; and ψ(z)=z^2/2 on[0,1] with center-1 outsideV and boundary minimum0. The ordered nonquadratic divergences are9/64 and11/64. Each universal comparison and separately selected final numerical proof branch retains actual public proximal_one_step VALUE; final bounds -1/2<=-5/16 and -1/2<=1/2 use equality transport of that comparison. Divergence formulas also use actual public gradient conversion. Nonnegative has a full generic public VALUE witness, with no claimed concrete Test VALUE use. These are illustrative instances, not new printed results, an existence theorem or a causal algorithm. A necessary Bregman foundation for the Chapter2 prescient forward dependency, not complete Algorithm15.8/Theorem15.30 or acceptance of Chapter6/15. Source X/interior and local-extension validity, finite-domain extended-real loss/subgradient/convexity/minimum bridges, attained causal current-loss recursion/interior invariants, and sharp fixed/variable same-run telescopes remain REQUIRED/OPEN, including the main-text fixed-step exercise. All eight Chapter2 forward containers remain open; Chapter2 partial, Chapters1–16 Goal ACTIVE. Stacked on OPEN draft unmerged PR208 exact 71f2219fa1648094eba8aa17b50e443258f436cb. No merge/deploy/main/live/CI acceptance claim. Actual BanditRL.OnlineProximal.convex_minimizer_comparison and own three_point_identity are compiled VALUE parents. Actual Mathlib HasFDerivAt.comp/sub/sub_const/const_smul and positive scalar multiplication differentiate the exact penalty.
